harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured port mirroring so node3 receives a copy of all traffic exchanged between node1 and node2 on their shared segment (eth1, 192.168.50.0/24), while the original node1<->node2 traffic continues unaffected. Implementation: node1 (the SONiC device, one of the two conversant hosts) runs a Linux tc clsact classifier on eth1 with two flower filters (matching frames to/from node2's MAC) that use a mirred "mirror" action (non-disruptive copy) to duplicate matching L2 frames into a GRE-tap (gretap) tunnel device 'mirror0'. That tunnel carries the mirrored copies over the separate management network (eth0, 10.100.40.0/24) to a matching gretap device on node3, where a capture on 'mirror0' shows the mirrored node1<->node2 packets even though node3 is not one of the two endpoints and its direct eth1 capture stays empty (confirming the segment is a real switched domain, not a hub, and that mirroring - not flooding - is responsible). Baseline testing (before mirroring) confirmed node3 saw zero node1<->node2 packets on eth1 directly; after mirroring was enabled, node3's mirror0 interface captured all ICMP request/reply pairs, and concurrent pings showed 0% packet loss, proving the original path was undisturbed. Required a fix for RHEL7's default firewalld/conntrack behavior: GRE (protocol 47) was being dropped as ctstate INVALID because nf_conntrack_proto_gre wasn't loaded; loading it (persisted via /etc/modules-load.d) plus a permanent firewalld protocol=gre allow resolved delivery to node3. All configuration (eth1 addressing, gretap devices, tc filters) was persisted via systemd oneshot services (node1: mirror-setup.service; node3: mirror-recv.service) and NetworkManager ifcfg files (node2, node3) so it survives reboot. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id + working mirror/traffic) on all three nodes, restarted node1, then node2, then node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, non-blocking ack), polled each until reachable again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified full mirroring/traffic health after each individual restart and once more after all three had cycled.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=SONiC-VS switch (Debian 13), node2/node3=RHEL7 hosts; eth0=10.100.40.0/24 management network (default, DHCP); eth1=unconfigured second NIC shared by all three nodes forming the isolated segment for this task
Installed tcpdump on node2 (via yum) and node3 (via binary copy from node2 over cluster SSH key, since node3 had no enabled yum repos)

Assigned static IPs on eth1 (node1=192.168.50.1, node2=192.168.50.2, node3=192.168.50.3) and confirmed baseline: node1<->node2 ICMP traffic worked, but was invisible on node3's eth1 capture (real switched segment, not a hub)
Created gretap tunnel 'mirror0' between node1 (local 10.100.40.10) and node3 (local 10.100.40.12) over the eth0 management network

Diagnosed and fixed GRE delivery failure: loaded nf_conntrack_proto_gre kernel module on node3 (RHEL7 firewalld dropped un-tracked GRE as ctstate INVALID) and added a permanent firewalld protocol=gre allow rule
Installed tc clsact qdisc + two flower filters on node1's eth1 (matching node2's src/dst MAC) with mirred 'egress mirror' action to mirror0, confirmed via tc -s filter show that matches incremented
Verified end-to-end: node3's mirror0 capture showed all node1<->node2 ICMP packets while node3's direct eth1 capture stayed empty, and node1<->node2 ping showed 0% packet loss throughout

Persisted configuration for reboot survival: /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 + mirror-setup.service/mirror-setup.sh on node1; ifcfg-eth1 on node2; ifcfg-eth1 + mirror-recv.service/mirror-recv.sh + /etc/modules-load.d/gre.conf + permanent firewalld gre rule on node3
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, eth1/mirror0 state, tc filters) on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via native reboot (background nohup ack), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified mirror-setup.service active, eth1/mirror0/tc filters auto-restored, all SONiC docker containers back up, and full mirroring re-verified
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1 IP auto-restored via ifcfg, and full mirroring re-verified

Restarted node3 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1/mirror0/mirror-recv.service/gre conntrack module/firewalld rule all auto-restored, and did a final full end-to-end verification (mirror0 capture shows traffic, eth1 direct capture empty, 0% ping loss) with all three nodes on their post-restart boot

evidence.summary: Ping from node1 to node2 over eth1 succeeded (0% loss) while a concurrent tcpdump on node3's eth1 captured zero of those ICMP packets
